Demi-Trolls — Pertorog / Pirtereg

Les Demi-Trolls, appelés Pertorog au singulier et Pirtereg au pluriel, sont issus d’un mélange entre Olog-hai et Hommes Variags. Plus petits et plus agiles que les Trolls Noirs, ils possèdent surtout une intelligence comparable à celle des Humains. Leur Culture transforme cette combinaison de puissance et d’intelligence en gardes d’élite, tueurs, éclaireurs, soldats et chefs de guerre capables d’agir avec une véritable autonomie.

Origine entre Variags et Olog-hai

Leur héritage réunit deux mondes. Du côté troll viennent puissance, apparence sombre et aptitude naturelle au combat ; du côté humain viennent intelligence, agilité relative et lien avec les Variags. La Culture n’est cependant ni une simple Culture variag ni une Culture Olog-hai réduite : elle correspond à un groupe spécifiquement élevé pour servir des maîtres puissants dans des rôles exigeant force, réflexion et autonomie.

Une Culture produite pour servir

Les Demi-Trolls ne développent pas de royaume ou d’institution autonome durable. Leur existence est organisée par les puissances qui les produisent et les emploient. La fonction est souvent attribuée : garde, soldat, éclaireur, exécuteur ou commandant. Cette absence de société propre donne une importance immense au maître, à la garnison et à la mission.

Intelligence et autonomie

Contrairement aux Trolls primitifs, un Demi-Troll peut recevoir une mission en plusieurs étapes, choisir un itinéraire, reconnaître une cible, interroger quelqu’un et modifier son plan lorsque les circonstances changent. Il peut devenir un véritable agent plutôt qu’une simple force de choc.

Gardes d’élite, tueurs et chefs de guerre

Comme garde du corps, il associe puissance et vigilance. Comme tueur, il doit rechercher une cible, suivre une piste et choisir le moment du combat. Certains deviennent chefs de guerre capables de commander Orcs, Hommes, mercenaires ou autres serviteurs de l’Ombre. Commandement, Tactique et Interrogatoire sont donc pleinement culturels.

Relations avec les autres Trolls

Les Demi-Trolls évitent généralement les autres Trolls. Ils sont assez proches physiquement pour rappeler leur origine, mais suffisamment plus rapides, intelligents et organisés pour que la coexistence soit difficile. L’Olog-hai reste un parent militaire plus proche, mais les fonctions diffèrent : l’Olog brise la ligne ; le Demi-Troll peut décider où elle doit être brisée.

Vêtements noirs

Leur apparence culturelle est sombre et militaire : tunique noire de cuir, laine ou soie, large ceinture ou bandoulière, protections de poignet, bottes et cape noire ou sombre. La couleur et la fonction comptent davantage qu’un matériau unique. Un garde de haut rang peut porter de la soie noire sous son armure ; un soldat davantage de cuir et de laine.

Armures lourdes

Toutes les catégories d’armure sont accessibles et la plate de métal noir est courante. Il ne faut pas attribuer automatiquement des propriétés magiques à ce métal : il s’agit d’abord d’un équipement militaire adapté à leur taille et à leur rôle. La Culture doit fortement développer l’usage des armures sans reproduire la protection naturelle raciale.

Arsenal polyvalent

L’arsenal est exceptionnellement large : haches, bolas, épées, arcs composites, arbalètes, dagues, fléaux, hallebardes, javelots, masses, cimeterres, épées à deux mains, marteaux, fouets, marteaux-pioches, armes de jet et autres variantes. Pour RMU, cette variété doit produire plusieurs spécialisations possibles plutôt qu’une maîtrise uniforme de toutes les armes.

Soldat, Éclaireur et Mercenaire

Les trois orientations les plus naturelles sont le Soldat, l’Éclaireur et le Mercenaire. Le Soldat développe armure, arme, Signalisation et discipline. L’Éclaireur privilégie Pistage, Observation, Approche furtive, Dissimulation, Embuscade, Escalade et techniques d’infiltration. Le Mercenaire apprend à fonctionner avec différents commandements et équipements.

Équitation et Dressage

L’Équitation et le Dressage sont culturellement accessibles, ce qui distingue fortement les Demi-Trolls des Tereg primitifs. Leur héritage variag fournit un contexte naturel à cette pratique. Les montures doivent évidemment être adaptées à leur masse. Des animaux liés aux forces de l’Ombre peuvent également être associés à certains individus selon les Talents disponibles.

Pistage, Embuscade et discrétion

Le Pistage sert au tueur et à l’éclaireur. Embuscade, Approche furtive et Dissimulation permettent de choisir le moment de l’affrontement. Leur grande taille reste une contrainte, mais leur agilité supérieure à celle des Olog-hai leur permet de développer réellement ces compétences, surtout avec un équipement plus léger.

Crochetage, pièges et Acrobaties

Crochetage et Désamorçage de pièges confirment une véritable capacité d’infiltration. Un Demi-Troll peut entrer autrement qu’en détruisant une porte. Acrobaties et Sprint traduisent culturellement leur mobilité supérieure sans reproduire les bonus physiques de la Race.

Observation, Premiers soins et Estimation

L’Observation sert autant au garde qu’au chef. Les Premiers soins permettent de stabiliser un compagnon et de maintenir une unité opérationnelle. L’Estimation aide le mercenaire à juger récompenses, armes et ressources. Ces compétences montrent une compréhension pratique beaucoup plus large que chez les Trolls ordinaires.

Artisanat militaire

Travail des métaux, Travail du cuir et Empennage assurent entretien et réparation des armes, armures, sangles et projectiles. Tous les Demi-Trolls ne sont pas artisans, mais les forces qui les emploient ont besoin de cette compétence pratique.

Signalisation, Commandement et Tactique

La Signalisation coordonne une force organisée. Le Commandement devient central chez les chefs de guerre ; la Tactique permet d’analyser un champ de bataille, choisir une position et préparer une embuscade. Leur intelligence humaine donne à ces compétences une profondeur supérieure à celle d’un Troll primitif.

Interrogatoire et Tromperie

L’Interrogatoire combine présence terrifiante et capacité à comprendre les réponses. La Tromperie permet de cacher un objectif ou manipuler un subordonné, même si l’apparence du Demi-Troll rend l’infiltration sociale beaucoup plus difficile que pour un Demi-Orc. La Séduction peut exister chez des individus particuliers sans devenir un axe central.

Religion noire

La Culture n’a pas de religion propre, mais peut apprendre les symboles, doctrines et usages des cultes noirs servis par son maître. La compétence correspond donc davantage à une connaissance pratique des religions de l’Ombre qu’à une foi collective obligatoire.

Langues

Le Parler Noir et le westron peuvent être maîtrisés à un haut niveau. Le varadja reflète l’origine variag ; le haradaic est utile dans les forces méridionales ; l’orcien permet de commander des Orcs. Cette polyvalence linguistique fait du Demi-Troll un excellent intermédiaire militaire.

Relations

Les Variags constituent l’un des principaux liens humains de la Culture. Les Orcs peuvent être commandés ou employés comme subordonnés ; les Olog-hai remplissent une fonction de force de choc complémentaire. Les Khazâd sont particulièrement haïs. Avec les autres Humains, la relation est complexe : le Demi-Troll parle leurs langues et comprend leur organisation, mais son apparence reste immédiatement distinctive.

Compétences culturelles

Le profil est très large : Armures, Armes, Escalade, Équitation, Pistage, Embuscade, Approche furtive, Dissimulation, Crochetage, Désamorçage de pièges, Observation, Développement corporel, Acrobaties, Dressage, Estimation, Spéléologie, Premiers soins, Signalisation, Tromperie, Lutte, Sprint, Travail des métaux, Travail du cuir, Empennage, Commandement, Interrogatoire et Tactique. Les rangs doivent être répartis selon la fonction plutôt qu’accumuler toutes ces compétences au maximum.

Race et Culture

La Race Demi-Trolls porte stature, peau noire, yeux rouges, vision, protection naturelle, longévité et résistance. La Culture Demi-Trolls porte vêtements noirs, armures, armes, langues, Équitation, Pistage, infiltration, Commandement, Tactique et fonctions militaires. Aucun avantage racial ne doit être répété.

Disponibilité et création

La Culture apparaît après 1200 du Troisième Âge et reste disponible au Quatrième. Un personnage doit définir pour qui il a été élevé, sa fonction — garde du corps, tueur, éclaireur, soldat ou chef de guerre — et son rapport aux Variags et aux Trolls. Après la chute des grandes puissances de l’Ombre, son intelligence et sa polyvalence lui permettent mieux qu’à beaucoup de Trolls de reconstruire une existence indépendante. La question centrale devient alors : que fait-il de capacités conçues pour servir lorsqu’il n’y a plus de maître ?

Langues de départ

  • Black Speech — Parlée 8 / Écrite 8
  • Westron — Parlée 6 / Écrite 6

Half-trolls — Pertorog / Pirtereg

Half-trolls, called Pertorog in the singular and Pirtereg in the plural, result from a mixture of Olog-hai and Variag Men. Smaller and more agile than Black Trolls, they above all possess intelligence comparable to that of Humans. Their Culture turns this combination of power and intelligence into elite guards, killers, scouts, soldiers, and war leaders capable of acting with genuine autonomy.

Origin between Variags and Olog-hai

Their heritage brings together two worlds. From the Troll side come power, dark appearance, and a natural aptitude for combat; from the human side come intelligence, relative agility, and a connection with the Variags. The Culture is nevertheless neither simply a Variag Culture nor a reduced Olog-hai Culture: it corresponds to a group specifically raised to serve powerful masters in roles requiring strength, thought, and autonomy.

A Culture produced to serve

Half-trolls do not develop a lasting independent kingdom or institution. Their existence is organized by the powers that produce and employ them. A function is often assigned: guard, soldier, scout, executioner, or commander. This absence of a society of their own gives enormous importance to master, garrison, and mission.

Intelligence and autonomy

Unlike primitive Trolls, a Half-troll can receive a multi-stage mission, choose a route, identify a target, question someone, and modify his plan when circumstances change. He can become a true agent rather than a mere shock force.

Elite guards, killers, and war leaders

As a bodyguard, he combines power and vigilance. As a killer, he must find a target, follow a trail, and choose the moment to fight. Some become war leaders capable of commanding Orcs, Men, mercenaries, or other servants of the Shadow. Leadership, Tactics, and Interrogation are therefore fully cultural skills.

Relations with other Trolls

Half-trolls generally avoid other Trolls. They are physically close enough to recall their origin, yet sufficiently faster, more intelligent, and more organized to make coexistence difficult. The Olog-hai remains a closer military relative, but their functions differ: the Olog breaks the line; the Half-troll can decide where it should be broken.

Black clothing

Their cultural appearance is dark and military: a black tunic of leather, wool, or silk, a broad belt or baldric, wrist guards, boots, and a black or dark cloak. Color and function matter more than any single material. A high-ranking guard may wear black silk beneath his armor; a soldier more often leather and wool.

Heavy armor

All armor categories are accessible, and black metal plate is common. No magical properties should automatically be attributed to this metal: it is first and foremost military equipment adapted to their size and role. The Culture should strongly develop armor use without reproducing racial natural protection.

Versatile arsenal

The arsenal is exceptionally broad: axes, bolas, swords, bows, composite bows, crossbows, daggers, flails, halberds, javelins, maces, scimitars, two-handed swords, hammers, whips, pick-hammers, thrown weapons, and other variants. For RMU, this variety should produce several possible specializations rather than uniform mastery of every weapon.

Soldier, Scout, and Mercenary

The three most natural orientations are Soldier, Scout, and Mercenary. The Soldier develops armor, weapon, Signaling, and discipline. The Scout emphasizes Tracking, Observation, Stalking, Hiding, Ambush, Climbing, and infiltration techniques. The Mercenary learns to function under different commands and with different equipment.

Riding and Animal Handling

Riding and Animal Handling are culturally accessible, strongly distinguishing Half-trolls from primitive Tereg. Their Variag heritage provides a natural context for this practice. Mounts must of course be suited to their mass. Animals associated with the forces of the Shadow may also accompany certain individuals depending on available Talents.

Tracking, Ambush, and stealth

Tracking serves the killer and scout. Ambush, Stalking, and Hiding allow the character to choose the moment of confrontation. Their great size remains a constraint, but their greater agility compared with Olog-hai allows them genuinely to develop these skills, especially with lighter equipment.

Lockpicking, traps, and Acrobatics

Lockpicking and Trap Disarming confirm a genuine capacity for infiltration. A Half-troll can enter without simply destroying a door. Acrobatics and Sprint culturally express their greater mobility without reproducing the Race's physical bonuses.

Observation, First Aid, and Appraisal

Observation serves both guard and leader. First Aid makes it possible to stabilize a companion and keep a unit operational. Appraisal helps the mercenary judge rewards, weapons, and resources. These skills demonstrate a much broader practical understanding than that of ordinary Trolls.

Military craft

Metalworking, Leatherworking, and Fletching provide maintenance and repair for weapons, armor, straps, and missiles. Not all Half-trolls are craftsmen, but the forces that employ them require this practical competence.

Signaling, Leadership, and Tactics

Signaling coordinates an organized force. Leadership becomes central among war leaders; Tactics allows them to analyze a battlefield, choose a position, and prepare an ambush. Their human-level intelligence gives these skills greater depth than they possess for a primitive Troll.

Interrogation and Deception

Interrogation combines terrifying presence with the ability to understand answers. Deception allows an objective to be concealed or a subordinate manipulated, even though a Half-troll's appearance makes social infiltration much more difficult than it is for a Half-orc. Seduction may exist among particular individuals without becoming a central focus.

Dark religion

The Culture has no religion of its own, but can learn the symbols, doctrines, and practices of the dark cults served by its master. The skill therefore represents practical knowledge of religions of the Shadow more than a mandatory collective faith.

Languages

The Black Speech and Westron can be mastered to a high level. Varadja reflects the Variag origin; Haradaic is useful in southern forces; Orcish allows Orcs to be commanded. This linguistic versatility makes a Half-troll an excellent military intermediary.

Relations

Variags form one of the Culture's main human connections. Orcs may be commanded or employed as subordinates; Olog-hai fulfill a complementary shock-force role. Khazâd are particularly hated. Relations with other Humans are complex: the Half-troll speaks their languages and understands their organization, but his appearance remains immediately distinctive.

Cultural skills

The profile is very broad: Armor, Weapons, Climbing, Riding, Tracking, Ambush, Stalking, Hiding, Lockpicking, Trap Disarming, Observation, Body Development, Acrobatics, Animal Handling, Appraisal, Caving, First Aid, Signaling, Deception, Wrestling, Sprint, Metalworking, Leatherworking, Fletching, Leadership, Interrogation, and Tactics. Ranks should be distributed according to function rather than maximizing all of these skills.

Race and Culture

The Half-troll Race carries stature, black skin, red eyes, vision, natural protection, longevity, and resistance. The Half-troll Culture carries black clothing, armor, weapons, languages, Riding, Tracking, infiltration, Leadership, Tactics, and military functions. No racial advantage should be repeated.

Availability and character creation

The Culture appears after 1200 of the Third Age and remains available in the Fourth. A character should define for whom he was raised, his function — bodyguard, killer, scout, soldier, or war leader — and his relationship with Variags and Trolls. After the fall of the great powers of the Shadow, his intelligence and versatility allow him, more readily than many Trolls, to rebuild an independent existence. The central question then becomes: what does he do with abilities designed for service when there is no longer a master?

  • Westron — Spoken 6 / Written 6

Half-trolls — Pertorog / Pirtereg

Half-trolls, called Pertorog in the singular and Pirtereg in the plural, result from a mixture of Olog-hai and Variag Men. Smaller and more agile than Black Trolls, they above all possess intelligence comparable to that of Humans. Their Culture turns this combination of power and intelligence into elite guards, killers, scouts, soldiers, and war leaders capable of acting with genuine autonomy.

Origin between Variags and Olog-hai

Their heritage brings together two worlds. From the Troll side come power, dark appearance, and a natural aptitude for combat; from the human side come intelligence, relative agility, and a connection with the Variags. The Culture is nevertheless neither simply a Variag Culture nor a reduced Olog-hai Culture: it corresponds to a group specifically raised to serve powerful masters in roles requiring strength, thought, and autonomy.

A Culture produced to serve

Half-trolls do not develop a lasting independent kingdom or institution. Their existence is organized by the powers that produce and employ them. A function is often assigned: guard, soldier, scout, executioner, or commander. This absence of a society of their own gives enormous importance to master, garrison, and mission.

Intelligence and autonomy

Unlike primitive Trolls, a Half-troll can receive a multi-stage mission, choose a route, identify a target, question someone, and modify his plan when circumstances change. He can become a true agent rather than a mere shock force.

Elite guards, killers, and war leaders

As a bodyguard, he combines power and vigilance. As a killer, he must find a target, follow a trail, and choose the moment to fight. Some become war leaders capable of commanding Orcs, Men, mercenaries, or other servants of the Shadow. Leadership, Tactics, and Interrogation are therefore fully cultural skills.

Relations with other Trolls

Half-trolls generally avoid other Trolls. They are physically close enough to recall their origin, yet sufficiently faster, more intelligent, and more organized to make coexistence difficult. The Olog-hai remains a closer military relative, but their functions differ: the Olog breaks the line; the Half-troll can decide where it should be broken.

Black clothing

Their cultural appearance is dark and military: a black tunic of leather, wool, or silk, a broad belt or baldric, wrist guards, boots, and a black or dark cloak. Color and function matter more than any single material. A high-ranking guard may wear black silk beneath his armor; a soldier more often leather and wool.

Heavy armor

All armor categories are accessible, and black metal plate is common. No magical properties should automatically be attributed to this metal: it is first and foremost military equipment adapted to their size and role. The Culture should strongly develop armor use without reproducing racial natural protection.

Versatile arsenal

The arsenal is exceptionally broad: axes, bolas, swords, bows, composite bows, crossbows, daggers, flails, halberds, javelins, maces, scimitars, two-handed swords, hammers, whips, pick-hammers, thrown weapons, and other variants. For RMU, this variety should produce several possible specializations rather than uniform mastery of every weapon.

Soldier, Scout, and Mercenary

The three most natural orientations are Soldier, Scout, and Mercenary. The Soldier develops armor, weapon, Signaling, and discipline. The Scout emphasizes Tracking, Observation, Stalking, Hiding, Ambush, Climbing, and infiltration techniques. The Mercenary learns to function under different commands and with different equipment.

Riding and Animal Handling

Riding and Animal Handling are culturally accessible, strongly distinguishing Half-trolls from primitive Tereg. Their Variag heritage provides a natural context for this practice. Mounts must of course be suited to their mass. Animals associated with the forces of the Shadow may also accompany certain individuals depending on available Talents.

Tracking, Ambush, and stealth

Tracking serves the killer and scout. Ambush, Stalking, and Hiding allow the character to choose the moment of confrontation. Their great size remains a constraint, but their greater agility compared with Olog-hai allows them genuinely to develop these skills, especially with lighter equipment.

Lockpicking, traps, and Acrobatics

Lockpicking and Trap Disarming confirm a genuine capacity for infiltration. A Half-troll can enter without simply destroying a door. Acrobatics and Sprint culturally express their greater mobility without reproducing the Race's physical bonuses.

Observation, First Aid, and Appraisal

Observation serves both guard and leader. First Aid makes it possible to stabilize a companion and keep a unit operational. Appraisal helps the mercenary judge rewards, weapons, and resources. These skills demonstrate a much broader practical understanding than that of ordinary Trolls.

Military craft

Metalworking, Leatherworking, and Fletching provide maintenance and repair for weapons, armor, straps, and missiles. Not all Half-trolls are craftsmen, but the forces that employ them require this practical competence.

Signaling, Leadership, and Tactics

Signaling coordinates an organized force. Leadership becomes central among war leaders; Tactics allows them to analyze a battlefield, choose a position, and prepare an ambush. Their human-level intelligence gives these skills greater depth than they possess for a primitive Troll.

Interrogation and Deception

Interrogation combines terrifying presence with the ability to understand answers. Deception allows an objective to be concealed or a subordinate manipulated, even though a Half-troll's appearance makes social infiltration much more difficult than it is for a Half-orc. Seduction may exist among particular individuals without becoming a central focus.

Dark religion

The Culture has no religion of its own, but can learn the symbols, doctrines, and practices of the dark cults served by its master. The skill therefore represents practical knowledge of religions of the Shadow more than a mandatory collective faith.

Languages

The Black Speech and Westron can be mastered to a high level. Varadja reflects the Variag origin; Haradaic is useful in southern forces; Orcish allows Orcs to be commanded. This linguistic versatility makes a Half-troll an excellent military intermediary.

Relations

Variags form one of the Culture's main human connections. Orcs may be commanded or employed as subordinates; Olog-hai fulfill a complementary shock-force role. Khazâd are particularly hated. Relations with other Humans are complex: the Half-troll speaks their languages and understands their organization, but his appearance remains immediately distinctive.

Cultural skills

The profile is very broad: Armor, Weapons, Climbing, Riding, Tracking, Ambush, Stalking, Hiding, Lockpicking, Trap Disarming, Observation, Body Development, Acrobatics, Animal Handling, Appraisal, Caving, First Aid, Signaling, Deception, Wrestling, Sprint, Metalworking, Leatherworking, Fletching, Leadership, Interrogation, and Tactics. Ranks should be distributed according to function rather than maximizing all of these skills.

Race and Culture

The Half-troll Race carries stature, black skin, red eyes, vision, natural protection, longevity, and resistance. The Half-troll Culture carries black clothing, armor, weapons, languages, Riding, Tracking, infiltration, Leadership, Tactics, and military functions. No racial advantage should be repeated.

Availability and character creation

The Culture appears after 1200 of the Third Age and remains available in the Fourth. A character should define for whom he was raised, his function — bodyguard, killer, scout, soldier, or war leader — and his relationship with Variags and Trolls. After the fall of the great powers of the Shadow, his intelligence and versatility allow him, more readily than many Trolls, to rebuild an independent existence. The central question then becomes: what does he do with abilities designed for service when there is no longer a master?

Metalworking, Leatherworking, and Fletching provide maintenance and repair for weapons, armor, straps, and missiles. Not all Half-trolls are craftsmen, but the forces that employ them require this practical competence.

Signaling coordinates an organized force. Leadership becomes central among war leaders; Tactics allows them to analyze a battlefield, choose a position, and prepare an ambush. Their human-level intelligence gives these skills greater depth than they possess for a primitive Troll.

Interrogation combines terrifying presence with the ability to understand answers. Cultural skills

Ranks should be distributed according to function rather than maximizing all of these skills.

Race and Culture

The Half-troll Race carries stature, black skin, red eyes, vision, natural protection, longevity, and resistance. The Half-troll Culture carries black clothing, armor, weapons, languages, Riding, Tracking, infiltration, Leadership, Tactics, and military functions. No racial advantage should be repeated.

Availability and character creation

The Culture appears after 1200 of the Third Age and remains available in the Fourth. A character should define for whom he was raised, his function — bodyguard, killer, scout, soldier, or war leader — and his relationship with Variags and Trolls. After the fall of the great powers of the Shadow, his intelligence and versatility allow him, more readily than many Trolls, to rebuild an independent existence. The central question then becomes: what does he do with abilities designed for service when there is no longer a master?

  • Westron — Spoken 6 / Written 6

Metalworking, Leatherworking, and Fletching provide maintenance and repair for weapons, armor, straps, and missiles. Not all Half-trolls are craftsmen, but the forces that employ them require this practical competence.

Signaling coordinates an organized force. Leadership becomes central among war leaders; Tactics allows them to analyze a battlefield, choose a position, and prepare an ambush. Their human-level intelligence gives these skills greater depth than they possess for a primitive Troll.

Interrogation combines terrifying presence with the ability to understand answers. The Culture has no religion of its own, but can learn the symbols, doctrines, and practices of the dark cults served by its master. The skill therefore represents practical knowledge of religions of the Shadow more than a mandatory collective faith.

The Black Speech and Westron can be mastered to a high level. Varadja reflects the Variag origin; Haradaic is useful in southern forces; Orcish allows Orcs to be commanded. This linguistic versatility makes a Half-troll an excellent military intermediary.

Variags form one of the Culture's main human connections. Orcs may be commanded or employed as subordinates; Olog-hai fulfill a complementary shock-force role. Khazâd are particularly hated. Relations with other Humans are complex: the Half-troll speaks their languages and understands their organization, but his appearance remains immediately distinctive.

Cultural skills

The profile is very broad: Armor, Weapons, Climbing, Riding, Tracking, Ambush, Stalking, Hiding, Lockpicking, Trap Disarming, Observation, Body Development, Acrobatics, Animal Handling, Appraisal, Caving, First Aid, Signaling, Deception, Wrestling, Sprint, Metalworking, Leatherworking, Fletching, Leadership, Interrogation, and Tactics. Ranks should be distributed according to function rather than maximizing all of these skills.

Race and Culture

The Half-troll Race carries stature, black skin, red eyes, vision, natural protection, longevity, and resistance. The Half-troll Culture carries black clothing, armor, weapons, languages, Riding, Tracking, infiltration, Leadership, Tactics, and military functions. No racial advantage should be repeated.

Availability and character creation

The Culture appears after 1200 of the Third Age and remains available in the Fourth. A character should define for whom he was raised, his function — bodyguard, killer, scout, soldier, or war leader — and his relationship with Variags and Trolls. After the fall of the great powers of the Shadow, his intelligence and versatility allow him, more readily than many Trolls, to rebuild an independent existence. The central question then becomes: what does he do with abilities designed for service when there is no longer a master?

  • Westron — Spoken 6 / Written 6

La Culture Demi-Trolls porte vêtements noirs, armures, armes, langues, Équitation, Pistage, infiltration, Commandement, Tactique et fonctions militaires. Aucun avantage racial ne doit être répété.

Disponibilité et création

La Culture apparaît après 1200 du Troisième Âge et reste disponible au Quatrième. Un personnage doit définir pour qui il a été élevé, sa fonction — garde du corps, tueur, éclaireur, soldat ou chef de guerre — et son rapport aux Variags et aux Trolls. Après la chute des grandes puissances de l’Ombre, son intelligence et sa polyvalence lui permettent mieux qu’à beaucoup de Trolls de reconstruire une existence indépendante. La question centrale devient alors : que fait-il de capacités conçues pour servir lorsqu’il n’y a plus de maître ?

Demi-Trolls — Pertorog / Pirtereg

Les Demi-Trolls, appelés Pertorog au singulier et Pirtereg au pluriel, sont issus d’un mélange entre Olog-hai et Hommes Variags. Plus petits et plus agiles que les Trolls Noirs, ils possèdent surtout une intelligence comparable à celle des Humains. Leur Culture transforme cette combinaison de puissance et d’intelligence en gardes d’élite, tueurs, éclaireurs, soldats et chefs de guerre capables d’agir avec une véritable autonomie.

Origine entre Variags et Olog-hai

Leur héritage réunit deux mondes. Du côté troll viennent puissance, apparence sombre et aptitude naturelle au combat ; du côté humain viennent intelligence, agilité relative et lien avec les Variags. La Culture n’est cependant ni une simple Culture variag ni une Culture Olog-hai réduite : elle correspond à un groupe spécifiquement élevé pour servir des maîtres puissants dans des rôles exigeant force, réflexion et autonomie.

Une Culture produite pour servir

Les Demi-Trolls ne développent pas de royaume ou d’institution autonome durable. Leur existence est organisée par les puissances qui les produisent et les emploient. La fonction est souvent attribuée : garde, soldat, éclaireur, exécuteur ou commandant. Cette absence de société propre donne une importance immense au maître, à la garnison et à la mission.

Intelligence et autonomie

Contrairement aux Trolls primitifs, un Demi-Troll peut recevoir une mission en plusieurs étapes, choisir un itinéraire, reconnaître une cible, interroger quelqu’un et modifier son plan lorsque les circonstances changent. Il peut devenir un véritable agent plutôt qu’une simple force de choc.

Gardes d’élite, tueurs et chefs de guerre

Comme garde du corps, il associe puissance et vigilance. Comme tueur, il doit rechercher une cible, suivre une piste et choisir le moment du combat. Certains deviennent chefs de guerre capables de commander Orcs, Hommes, mercenaires ou autres serviteurs de l’Ombre. Commandement, Tactique et Interrogatoire sont donc pleinement culturels.

Relations avec les autres Trolls

Les Demi-Trolls évitent généralement les autres Trolls. Ils sont assez proches physiquement pour rappeler leur origine, mais suffisamment plus rapides, intelligents et organisés pour que la coexistence soit difficile. L’Olog-hai reste un parent militaire plus proche, mais les fonctions diffèrent : l’Olog brise la ligne ; le Demi-Troll peut décider où elle doit être brisée.

Vêtements noirs

Leur apparence culturelle est sombre et militaire : tunique noire de cuir, laine ou soie, large ceinture ou bandoulière, protections de poignet, bottes et cape noire ou sombre. La couleur et la fonction comptent davantage qu’un matériau unique. Un garde de haut rang peut porter de la soie noire sous son armure ; un soldat davantage de cuir et de laine.

Armures lourdes

Toutes les catégories d’armure sont accessibles et la plate de métal noir est courante. Il ne faut pas attribuer automatiquement des propriétés magiques à ce métal : il s’agit d’abord d’un équipement militaire adapté à leur taille et à leur rôle. La Culture doit fortement développer l’usage des armures sans reproduire la protection naturelle raciale.

Arsenal polyvalent

L’arsenal est exceptionnellement large : haches, bolas, épées, arcs composites, arbalètes, dagues, fléaux, hallebardes, javelots, masses, cimeterres, épées à deux mains, marteaux, fouets, marteaux-pioches, armes de jet et autres variantes. Pour RMU, cette variété doit produire plusieurs spécialisations possibles plutôt qu’une maîtrise uniforme de toutes les armes.

Soldat, Éclaireur et Mercenaire

Les trois orientations les plus naturelles sont le Soldat, l’Éclaireur et le Mercenaire. Le Soldat développe armure, arme, Signalisation et discipline. L’Éclaireur privilégie Pistage, Observation, Approche furtive, Dissimulation, Embuscade, Escalade et techniques d’infiltration. Le Mercenaire apprend à fonctionner avec différents commandements et équipements.

Équitation et Dressage

L’Équitation et le Dressage sont culturellement accessibles, ce qui distingue fortement les Demi-Trolls des Tereg primitifs. Leur héritage variag fournit un contexte naturel à cette pratique. Les montures doivent évidemment être adaptées à leur masse. Des animaux liés aux forces de l’Ombre peuvent également être associés à certains individus selon les Talents disponibles.

Pistage, Embuscade et discrétion

Le Pistage sert au tueur et à l’éclaireur. Embuscade, Approche furtive et Dissimulation permettent de choisir le moment de l’affrontement. Leur grande taille reste une contrainte, mais leur agilité supérieure à celle des Olog-hai leur permet de développer réellement ces compétences, surtout avec un équipement plus léger.

Crochetage, pièges et Acrobaties

Crochetage et Désamorçage de pièges confirment une véritable capacité d’infiltration. Un Demi-Troll peut entrer autrement qu’en détruisant une porte. Acrobaties et Sprint traduisent culturellement leur mobilité supérieure sans reproduire les bonus physiques de la Race.

Observation, Premiers soins et Estimation

L’Observation sert autant au garde qu’au chef. Les Premiers soins permettent de stabiliser un compagnon et de maintenir une unité opérationnelle. L’Estimation aide le mercenaire à juger récompenses, armes et ressources. Ces compétences montrent une compréhension pratique beaucoup plus large que chez les Trolls ordinaires.

Artisanat militaire

Travail des métaux, Travail du cuir et Empennage assurent entretien et réparation des armes, armures, sangles et projectiles. Tous les Demi-Trolls ne sont pas artisans, mais les forces qui les emploient ont besoin de cette compétence pratique.

Signalisation, Commandement et Tactique

La Signalisation coordonne une force organisée. Le Commandement devient central chez les chefs de guerre ; la Tactique permet d’analyser un champ de bataille, choisir une position et préparer une embuscade. Leur intelligence humaine donne à ces compétences une profondeur supérieure à celle d’un Troll primitif.

Interrogatoire et Tromperie

L’Interrogatoire combine présence terrifiante et capacité à comprendre les réponses. La Tromperie permet de cacher un objectif ou manipuler un subordonné, même si l’apparence du Demi-Troll rend l’infiltration sociale beaucoup plus difficile que pour un Demi-Orc. La Séduction peut exister chez des individus particuliers sans devenir un axe central.

Religion noire

La Culture n’a pas de religion propre, mais peut apprendre les symboles, doctrines et usages des cultes noirs servis par son maître. La compétence correspond donc davantage à une connaissance pratique des religions de l’Ombre qu’à une foi collective obligatoire.

Langues

Le Parler Noir et le westron peuvent être maîtrisés à un haut niveau. Le varadja reflète l’origine variag ; le haradaic est utile dans les forces méridionales ; l’orcien permet de commander des Orcs. Cette polyvalence linguistique fait du Demi-Troll un excellent intermédiaire militaire.

Relations

Les Variags constituent l’un des principaux liens humains de la Culture. Les Orcs peuvent être commandés ou employés comme subordonnés ; les Olog-hai remplissent une fonction de force de choc complémentaire. Les Khazâd sont particulièrement haïs. Avec les autres Humains, la relation est complexe : le Demi-Troll parle leurs langues et comprend leur organisation, mais son apparence reste immédiatement distinctive.

Compétences culturelles

Le profil est très large : Armures, Armes, Escalade, Équitation, Pistage, Embuscade, Approche furtive, Dissimulation, Crochetage, Désamorçage de pièges, Observation, Développement corporel, Acrobaties, Dressage, Estimation, Spéléologie, Premiers soins, Signalisation, Tromperie, Lutte, Sprint, Travail des métaux, Travail du cuir, Empennage, Commandement, Interrogatoire et Tactique. Les rangs doivent être répartis selon la fonction plutôt qu’accumuler toutes ces compétences au maximum.

Half-trolls — Pertorog / Pirtereg

Half-trolls, called Pertorog in the singular and Pirtereg in the plural, result from a mixture of Olog-hai and Variag Men. Smaller and more agile than Black Trolls, they above all possess intelligence comparable to that of Humans. Their Culture turns this combination of power and intelligence into elite guards, killers, scouts, soldiers, and war leaders capable of acting with genuine autonomy.

Origin between Variags and Olog-hai

Their heritage brings together two worlds. From the Troll side come power, dark appearance, and a natural aptitude for combat; from the human side come intelligence, relative agility, and a connection with the Variags. The Culture is nevertheless neither simply a Variag Culture nor a reduced Olog-hai Culture: it corresponds to a group specifically raised to serve powerful masters in roles requiring strength, thought, and autonomy.

A Culture produced to serve

Half-trolls do not develop a lasting independent kingdom or institution. Their existence is organized by the powers that produce and employ them. A function is often assigned: guard, soldier, scout, executioner, or commander. This absence of a society of their own gives enormous importance to master, garrison, and mission.

Intelligence and autonomy

Unlike primitive Trolls, a Half-troll can receive a multi-stage mission, choose a route, identify a target, question someone, and modify his plan when circumstances change. He can become a true agent rather than a mere shock force.

Elite guards, killers, and war leaders

As a bodyguard, he combines power and vigilance. As a killer, he must find a target, follow a trail, and choose the moment to fight. Some become war leaders capable of commanding Orcs, Men, mercenaries, or other servants of the Shadow. Leadership, Tactics, and Interrogation are therefore fully cultural skills.

Relations with other Trolls

Half-trolls generally avoid other Trolls. They are physically close enough to recall their origin, yet sufficiently faster, more intelligent, and more organized to make coexistence difficult. The Olog-hai remains a closer military relative, but their functions differ: the Olog breaks the line; the Half-troll can decide where it should be broken.

Black clothing

Their cultural appearance is dark and military: a black tunic of leather, wool, or silk, a broad belt or baldric, wrist guards, boots, and a black or dark cloak. Color and function matter more than any single material. A high-ranking guard may wear black silk beneath his armor; a soldier more often leather and wool.

Heavy armor

All armor categories are accessible, and black metal plate is common. No magical properties should automatically be attributed to this metal: it is first and foremost military equipment adapted to their size and role. The Culture should strongly develop armor use without reproducing racial natural protection.

Versatile arsenal

The arsenal is exceptionally broad: axes, bolas, swords, bows, composite bows, crossbows, daggers, flails, halberds, javelins, maces, scimitars, two-handed swords, hammers, whips, pick-hammers, thrown weapons, and other variants. For RMU, this variety should produce several possible specializations rather than uniform mastery of every weapon.

Soldier, Scout, and Mercenary

The three most natural orientations are Soldier, Scout, and Mercenary. The Soldier develops armor, weapon, Signaling, and discipline. The Scout emphasizes Tracking, Observation, Stalking, Hiding, Ambush, Climbing, and infiltration techniques. The Mercenary learns to function under different commands and with different equipment.

Riding and Animal Handling

Riding and Animal Handling are culturally accessible, strongly distinguishing Half-trolls from primitive Tereg. Their Variag heritage provides a natural context for this practice. Mounts must of course be suited to their mass. Animals associated with the forces of the Shadow may also accompany certain individuals depending on available Talents.

Tracking, Ambush, and stealth

Tracking serves the killer and scout. Ambush, Stalking, and Hiding allow the character to choose the moment of confrontation. Their great size remains a constraint, but their greater agility compared with Olog-hai allows them genuinely to develop these skills, especially with lighter equipment.

Lockpicking, traps, and Acrobatics

Lockpicking and Trap Disarming confirm a genuine capacity for infiltration. A Half-troll can enter without simply destroying a door. Acrobatics and Sprint culturally express their greater mobility without reproducing the Race's physical bonuses.

Observation, First Aid, and Appraisal

Observation serves both guard and leader. First Aid makes it possible to stabilize a companion and keep a unit operational. Appraisal helps the mercenary judge rewards, weapons, and resources. These skills demonstrate a much broader practical understanding than that of ordinary Trolls.

Military craft

Metalworking, Leatherworking, and Fletching provide maintenance and repair for weapons, armor, straps, and missiles. Not all Half-trolls are craftsmen, but the forces that employ them require this practical competence.

Signaling, Leadership, and Tactics

Signaling coordinates an organized force. Leadership becomes central among war leaders; Tactics allows them to analyze a battlefield, choose a position, and prepare an ambush. Their human-level intelligence gives these skills greater depth than they possess for a primitive Troll.

Interrogation and Deception

Interrogation combines terrifying presence with the ability to understand answers. Deception allows an objective to be concealed or a subordinate manipulated, even though a Half-troll's appearance makes social infiltration much more difficult than it is for a Half-orc. Seduction may exist among particular individuals without becoming a central focus.

Dark religion

The Culture has no religion of its own, but can learn the symbols, doctrines, and practices of the dark cults served by its master. The skill therefore represents practical knowledge of religions of the Shadow more than a mandatory collective faith.

Languages

The Black Speech and Westron can be mastered to a high level. Varadja reflects the Variag origin; Haradaic is useful in southern forces; Orcish allows Orcs to be commanded. This linguistic versatility makes a Half-troll an excellent military intermediary.

Relations

Variags form one of the Culture's main human connections. Orcs may be commanded or employed as subordinates; Olog-hai fulfill a complementary shock-force role. Khazâd are particularly hated. Relations with other Humans are complex: the Half-troll speaks their languages and understands their organization, but his appearance remains immediately distinctive.

Cultural skills

The profile is very broad: Armor, Weapons, Climbing, Riding, Tracking, Ambush, Stalking, Hiding, Lockpicking, Trap Disarming, Observation, Body Development, Acrobatics, Animal Handling, Appraisal, Caving, First Aid, Signaling, Deception, Wrestling, Sprint, Metalworking, Leatherworking, Fletching, Leadership, Interrogation, and Tactics. Ranks should be distributed according to function rather than maximizing all of these skills.

Race and Culture

The Half-troll Race carries stature, black skin, red eyes, vision, natural protection, longevity, and resistance. The Half-troll Culture carries black clothing, armor, weapons, languages, Riding, Tracking, infiltration, Leadership, Tactics, and military functions. No racial advantage should be repeated.

Availability and character creation

The Culture appears after 1200 of the Third Age and remains available in the Fourth. A character should define for whom he was raised, his function — bodyguard, killer, scout, soldier, or war leader — and his relationship with Variags and Trolls. After the fall of the great powers of the Shadow, his intelligence and versatility allow him, more readily than many Trolls, to rebuild an independent existence. The central question then becomes: what does he do with abilities designed for service when there is no longer a master?
